feature: HER2 (IHC 3+, discordant with weak research-grade MXIF) — ADC axis

rationale: The validated stain was already drawn in 2026-08 and only its tier is missing from the record, so the first move is retrieving that report rather than cutting a new slide. Without the tier, a poorly tolerated T-DXd course continues on three-year-old tissue, and a genuine drop to HER2-low moves the drug off its tumor-agnostic label, which is written for IHC 3+, and onto a bystander-payload argument.

tissue_required_estimate: Archival FFPE acceptable; already-cut 2026-08 material preferred, otherwise one block cut (2026-08 nodal core or 2025-03 recurrence) with tumor content stated on the report

feature: PRAME + HLA-A*02:01 — ImmTAC/TCR axis, pending expression
test_name: PRAME expression by validated IHC (clone EPR20330) or RT-PCR, scored at the threshold the candidate protocol names

The MAGE-A4 sequence is the precedent: HLA matched, expression negative, option closed by a test rather than by assumption.

tissue_required_estimate: Archival FFPE block or 5-10 unstained slides; RT-PCR tolerates the 5-10% tumor content of the nodal cores better than IHC scoring

feature: TMB 12.4 mut/Mb + ongoing immune sensitivity — checkpoint re-intensification (ipilimumab addition)

Recomputing from the whole-exome sequencing already performed costs no tissue and settles whether the number survives a cross-assay comparison. It matters less for pembrolizumab, which this patient has already progressed through, than for trials that gate on a named assay and for the neoantigen argument behind the vaccine and ipilimumab-addition strategies.

feature: TMB 12.4 mut/Mb + ongoing immune sensitivity — checkpoint re-intensification (ipilimumab addition)
test_name: PD-L1 IHC by the companion clone a candidate protocol names (22C3 pharmDx or equivalent), on contemporary tissue
tissue_type: Archival FFPE, ideally the 2025-03 recurrence or the 2026-08 node
rationale: The two results on file are CPS 5 on the primary and CPS 0 in the liver metastasis, which is discordance rather than a number, and both date from 2023 on a laboratory clone validated as comparable to 22C3 rather than the companion assay itself. Checkpoint use in metastatic urothelial carcinoma is not PD-L1 gated, and this patient has already had both a deep response and progression on PD-1 blockade, so the practical weight is low. Repeat it when a specific protocol names a clone and a cutoff, not before.
turnaround_estimate: 3-7 days
tissue_required_estimate: Archival FFPE acceptable; one slide on the shared block cut when a protocol requires it
decision_gated: Entry to trials that specify a PD-L1 clone and cutoff; not a gate on checkpoint use itself.

providers.name: Labcorp Oncology
providers.notes: Runs the 22C3 companion assay at scale, which is what a protocol specifying CPS will accept; a laboratory-developed comparable clone is what left the current result unusable.

notes: The primary-versus-metastasis discordance is itself the finding, and it argues against reading any single CPS value as the tumor's state.

feature: PRAME + HLA-A*02:01 — ImmTAC/TCR axis, pending expression
test_name: Tumor HLA class I loss of heterozygosity computed from the existing tumor/normal exome data (LOHHLA or equivalent)
tissue_type: None; analysis of existing sequencing data
rationale: Germline typing is on file and positive for A*02:01, but somatic loss of that allele in the tumor would blunt every HLA-restricted approach in play here, from PRAME ImmTAC and TCR-T to the personalized neoantigen vaccines. The tumor and normal exome data needed for the calculation already exists, so this is an analysis rather than a specimen request. Skipping it leaves a class-wide escape mechanism unexamined while several A*02:01-dependent programs are being pursued.
turnaround_estimate: 1-2 weeks once the sequence data is in hand
tissue_required_estimate: No specimen; computed from existing tumor and normal exome data
decision_gated: Whether HLA-A*02:01-restricted approaches (PRAME ImmTAC / TCR-T, neoantigen vaccine) remain mechanistically plausible.
notes: This is a research-grade computation rather than a clinical assay, so it informs how the axis is ranked and would not be accepted as protocol eligibility evidence. It is separate from germline genotype, which the 2025-01 typing already settled.

feature: TMB 12.4 mut/Mb + ongoing immune sensitivity — checkpoint re-intensification (ipilimumab addition)
test_name: CD3, CD8 and macrophage density re-queried from the 2026-08 multiplex immunofluorescence run already performed on the nodal tissue
tissue_type: None; re-analysis of existing multiplex image data
rationale: The multiplex panel has already been run on the 2026-08 node, so immune-infiltrate density can be read from the existing image data at no tissue cost. An inflamed node supports adding CTLA-4 blockade or an IL-15 superagonist after progression on PD-1 maintenance, while an immune-desert pattern argues the problem is priming rather than checkpoint restraint. This is a research-grade readout that informs how the immune-intensification axis is ranked, not protocol eligibility.
turnaround_estimate: 1-2 weeks, analysis only
tissue_required_estimate: No specimen; re-analysis of the 2026-08 multiplex images already acquired
decision_gated: How the checkpoint re-intensification axis (ipilimumab addition, NK cells plus N-803) is weighted after progression on PD-1 maintenance.
notes: Ask the vendor whether the 2026-08 panel included T-cell and myeloid markers; if it was a tumor-antigen-only panel, this becomes a new stain and should join the shared block cut instead. Post-SBRT nodal tissue carries treatment-related inflammation, which complicates reading infiltrate density as baseline immune state.

feature: Mesothelin (strong on research-grade MXIF) — CAR-T/TCE/ADC trial axis, hedged
test_name: Serum soluble mesothelin-related peptide (SMRP) immunoassay
tissue_type: Serum; no tumor tissue
rationale: Shed mesothelin acts as a sink that blunts mesothelin-directed agents, so a soluble level is worth having before a CAR-T or engager protocol, and it needs blood rather than tissue. The assay is cleared for mesothelioma monitoring rather than for urothelial carcinoma, so a level here corroborates or undercuts the tissue call without replacing it. Low value on its own; it earns a line because it rides on a routine draw.
turnaround_estimate: 1 week
tissue_required_estimate: 3-5 mL serum on a routine draw; no tumor tissue
decision_gated: Refines the mesothelin target call and flags soluble-antigen sink before a mesothelin cell-therapy protocol.

feature: FAP-positive stroma — imaging/theranostic axis, heavily hedged
test_name: Retrieval of the 2026-06 FAP-directed imaging read, with quantitative FAPI PET uptake in the known nodal disease only if that read is uninformative
tissue_type: None
rationale: The one FAPI PET on record found no FAP-avid urothelial disease and lit up granulomatous prostate tissue instead, a classic false positive, so stromal positivity on an unvalidated multiplex assay does not make this a treatment lead. The 2026-06 repeat study has already been performed and its read costs nothing to retrieve. Recent SBRT to the nodal disease adds treatment-related fibroblast activation, which makes any new uptake harder to attribute to tumor stroma.
turnaround_estimate: Days for the retrieval; 2-4 weeks to arrange a new research FAPI PET
tissue_required_estimate: No specimen; imaging only
decision_gated: Whether FAP-directed radioligand concepts stay on the list; currently an imaging-research lead rather than a treatment lead.

providers.name: UCLA Health, Ahmanson Translational Theranostics Division
providers.notes: Runs gallium-68 FAPI-46 imaging studies through its theranostics program. FAPI PET is not FDA approved, so US access is by trial enrollment rather than a clinical order, and no formal expanded-access route was found.

providers.name: Stanford Nuclear Medicine and Molecular Imaging
providers.notes: Runs fluorine-18 FAPI-74 PET imaging studies; check current protocol openings and tumor-type eligibility.

notes: FAPI PET is not FDA approved and is available in the US mainly on research protocols, so a repeat study means an enrolling site rather than a clinical order.
